prompt: Implement cache_events(events) in a standalone standard-library Python file. All arguments are required. Model a local cache from an empty state: missing key generations are0, entries and pending fills are empty, and each call starts afresh. events must be a native list of at most128 native dicts with exactly the keys for their operation. IDs are native str values (exact built-in type, subclasses rejected), containing only ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, length1..32. The op field must also be a native str. Values are native integers (not bool) in [-1000,1000]. Operations: {"op":"begin","fill":id,"key":id,"value":int} captures the key's current generation/value in a pending fill; every fill ID must be unique throughout this call. {"op":"invalidate","key":id} increments that key's retained integer generation and deletes its entry, even if absent. {"op":"evict","key":id} deletes only the entry, retaining generation. {"op":"finish","fill":id} requires a pending fill, removes it, and atomically installs its value iff captured generation equals the key's current generation. {"op":"read","key":id} reads the entry or None. After each event append a native dict with exactly result, generations, entries, pending. result is a native bool only for finish, the native int value or None for read, and None otherwise. generations contains each key introduced by begin/invalidate/evict/read mapped to its retained generation. entries maps stored keys to int values. pending maps fill IDs to dicts with exactly key (str), generation (int), value (int). Return the native list of snapshots. All mutable containers must be independent within/across snapshots and calls, and from inputs; never mutate current or earlier inputs/results. Reject any invalid type/schema/domain, reused fill ID, or unknown finish with ValueError, with no partial result. This generation gate protects observed local invalidations; matching epochs do not prove origin freshness.

Implement bucket_events(capacity, initial, rate_num, rate_den, events) in a standalone standard-library Python file. All arguments required; all numeric inputs are native integers, never bool. capacity is0..100, initial is0..capacity, rate_num is0..100, rate_den is1..100. These define an exact continuous token bucket in token/time units; start at time0 with initial tokens and refill rate rate_num/rate_den. events is a native list of at most128 native dicts with exactly time and cost. time is0..1000000 and nondecreasing; cost is1..1000 tokens. Before each event add exact refill since the previous event and clamp balance at capacity; advance the accounting timestamp on every event, including refusals. Admit iff balance>=cost, then subtract cost; otherwise leave the refilled balance unchanged. No refunds, bypasses, or hidden resets. Return a native list of dicts with exactly accepted (native bool) and balance (a fresh two-element native int list [numerator,denominator], reduced, denominator positive). Use exact arithmetic, not floating approximations. Empty events returns[]. All mutable containers must be independent within/across outputs and calls and from inputs. Never mutate current/earlier inputs or results, including on errors. Invalid type/schema/domain or decreasing time raises ValueError with no partial result. The bucket constrains charged admitted tokens, not all offered requests or active worker lifetime.

Implement breaker_events(cooldown, events) in a standalone standard-library Python file. All arguments required. cooldown is a native int1..1000, not bool. events is a native list<=128 of exact-schema native dicts, with native int time0..1000000 nondecreasing. The op, id and outcome fields must be native str values, not subclasses. Start each call Closed, generation0, open_until=None, no active calls. Before EVERY event, if Open and time>=open_until, transition to HalfOpen, increment generation, clear open_until. {"op":"trip","time":t} represents an already-qualified failure signal: increment generation, enter Open, set open_until=t+cooldown, retain all active older calls. {"op":"call","time":t,"id":s} requires a unique call ID throughout this trace; ASCII letters/digits/hyphens/underscores, length1..32. Closed admits an ordinary active call with current generation and trial=False. Open refuses it. HalfOpen admits a trial iff no current-generation trial is active, otherwise refuses. Admitted calls retain their records until result; mode changes never free them. {"op":"result","time":t,"id":s,"outcome":"success"|"failure"} requires an active admitted call and removes it to represent actual work termination. Only a trial whose stored generation equals the current generation while mode is HalfOpen may change mode: success enters Closed with generation incremented/open_until=None; failure enters Open with generation incremented/open_until=t+cooldown. Other results, including stale successes, have no mode effect. Ordinary Closed results do not trip automatically; trip is the explicit input for that separate policy. {"op":"observe","time":t} has no other action. After each event return a fresh snapshot with exactly mode (Closed/Open/HalfOpen), generation (native int), open_until (native int or None), result (native bool for call admission, otherwise None), active (dict ID->dict with exactly generation:int, trial:bool). Return the native list of snapshots. Independent mutable containers within/across snapshots/calls and from inputs are required; never mutate earlier inputs/results, including on errors. Invalid types, schema, domains, decreasing times, reused call IDs, or unknown/refused/completed result IDs raise ValueError without partial result. The single current-generation trial cap excludes older work still active.

Implement queue_epochs(capacity, healthy, degraded, enter, exit, arrivals) in a standalone standard-library Python file. All arguments required. Every numeric input is a native int, never bool. capacity is2..100;1<=healthy<capacity;0<=degraded<healthy;0<=exit<enter<=capacity-healthy. arrivals is a native list<=128 of offered nonnegative integer counts0..1000, one per epoch. Start every call with empty waiting queue Q=0 and mode Healthy. For each offered count A: admit min(A,capacity-Q), reject the remainder; then complete up to healthy jobs if the mode at epoch start is Healthy, otherwise up to degraded, limited by available queued jobs. Compute the post-service queue, then transition Healthy->Degraded iff Q>=enter, or Degraded->Healthy iff Q<=exit. No other mode transition is allowed; service for an epoch uses its starting mode, not its ending mode. Return a native list of independent dict snapshots with exactly queue (int), mode (Healthy/Degraded), admitted (int), rejected (int), completed (int). Empty arrivals returns[]. Never mutate current/earlier inputs or outputs; all mutable containers independent across snapshots/calls and from inputs. Any invalid type/domain raises ValueError without partial result. Ordinary offered load below healthy capacity does not automatically restore healthy service after a trigger: recovery must drain using degraded capacity until the exit threshold. This is the explicit finite epoch model, not a prediction for all production queues.

Implement slo_report(shards, target_num, target_den, exception) in a standalone standard-library Python file. All arguments required. shards is a native list<=64 of exact native dicts with good and eligible native integers, never bool, satisfying0<=good<=eligible<=1000000. Schema field names must be native str, not subclasses. Cohorts are disjoint, use the same binary classifier and window, and count logical operations once. target_den is native int1..1000 and target_num is native int0..target_den; exception is a native bool authorizing the declared release exception. Pool G=sum(good),N=sum(eligible),B=N-G; target S=target_num/target_den. Return a fresh native dict with exactly eligible,good,bad (native ints), sli,allowance,remaining,burn (exact reduced [numerator,denominator] native int lists or specified None), met (native bool or None), release (native bool). sli=G/N for N>0, otherwise None. allowance=(1-S)*N even if fractional; remaining=allowance-B, retaining negative values. met reports G/N>=S for N>0, otherwise None. burn=(B/N)/(1-S) only when N>0 and S<1, otherwise None. All defined rational lists have positive denominators and must be independent within/across results/calls and from inputs. The selected release gate admits iff remaining>0 OR exception; all unrelated checks are assumed to pass, even for an empty population. Thus remaining0 can meet the SLO while refusing an ordinary release. Use exact arithmetic, not binary floats, floored allowance, unweighted shard means, or negative-budget clamping. Never mutate current/earlier inputs/results, including errors. Any invalid native type/schema/domain raises ValueError. This computes observed quantities and permission; it performs no deployment and predicts no future exhaustion time.
